# Implementation Plan: crews envelope summary canonical cleanup

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-31. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Retire one half of v1.7.3's defensive dual-path for the `summary` envelope field now
that v2.3.0+ has codified `env.summary` as the canonical wire address and the
`validateSummaryCanonical` silent-drop guard in `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` enforces
it (warn-mode in production, throw under `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` in CI as of v2.4.0).

**Decision: delete the CONSUMER FALLBACK at `hooks/commands/review-mail.js:110`**
(the `?? row?.payload?.summary` coalesce). Keep the producer mirror at
`hooks/stop.js:1086` and `:1122` as the transitional bridge for in-flight on-disk
envelopes. Bump crews to **v2.4.1** (patch). Survey of the other v1.7.3-era fields
(`kind`, `replyTo`, `decision`, `ack`, `progressTail`, `reviewedSeq`,
`bodyResolution`) confirms only `summary` has the defensive dual-path pattern; no
additional cleanups are in scope for this task. One adjacent finding —
`payload.kind` is write-mirrored at `stop.js:1087` and `:1123` with **zero
production reader** — is noted as a follow-up backlog item, not as part of v2.4.1.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

Canonical source: `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/` at HEAD `87e5dcc1`
(v2.4.0, `feat(crews): enable CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1 by default in CI`).

Producer mirror (v1.7.3 origin) — `payload.summary` is written alongside top-level
`summary` at TWO call-sites in `hooks/stop.js`:

| Location | Routing kind | Top-level `summary` | Payload mirror |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hooks/stop.js:1077-1089` | `member-reply` system-mailbox notification | line 1079 `summary: row.summary` | line 1086 `summary: row.summary` |
| `hooks/stop.js:1117-1137` | `proactive-report` system-mailbox notification | line 1132 `summary: latestTerminal.summary || null` | line 1122 `summary: latestTerminal.summary || null` (also line 1123 `kind: latestTerminal.kind` mirror) |

Consumer fallback (v1.7.3 origin) — single call-site:

- `hooks/commands/review-mail.js:110` — `summary: row?.summary ?? row?.payload?.summary ?? null`.
  This is the ONLY production consumer that reads `payload.summary`. A repo-wide
  grep across `hooks/**/*.js` for `payload.summary` / `payload?.summary` returns
  this line plus the envelope-validator comments in `hooks/protocol/envelope.js`.
  No other production reader exists.

Canonical-address enforcement (v2.3.0+) lives at `hooks/protocol/envelope.js`:

- Lines 16-20 — canonical-address contract: `summary` is `env.summary` (top-level);
  `payload.summary` is a "TRANSITIONAL DUPLICATE tolerated only when top-level
  `summary` is ALSO set; missing top-level + present payload.summary trips the
  silent-drop guard (v1.7.2 regression)".
- Lines 189-208 — `validateSummaryCanonical` implements that guard: throws under
  strict mode, emits `schema-warning:` log line in warn mode.
- Header comment line 192 explicitly anticipates this cleanup:
  *"The cleanup follow-up removes payload.summary entirely; until then this is
  the transitional bridge that locks the v1.7.2 regression in place."*
- v2.3.2 (`095bba57`) made `appendMailbox` a self-validating chokepoint, closing
  the last bypass path. v2.4.0 (`87e5dcc1`) made `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` the CI
  default. Together these mean any new producer that fails to set top-level
  `summary` fails its PR.

Tests that codify the dual-path (must change):

- `tests/review-mail-command.test.js:361-378` — explicitly constructs an envelope
  with `payload.summary` only (no top-level) and asserts
  `entry.summary === payloadSummary` ("`payload.summary` is used when top-level
  summary is absent"). This test EXISTS to codify the consumer fallback; removing
  the fallback requires inverting this test (now asserts `entry.summary === null`
  for payload-only input — and ideally constructs the row with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=0`
  to avoid the silent-drop guard tripping during the test fixture build).
- `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js:129-end` — the v1.7.2 regression
  test has TWO halves: (a) validator strict-mode rejection of payload-only
  summary, (b) consumer-fallback assertion that "the read-fallback at
  `review-mail.js:111` still surfaces the summary so legacy on-disk envelopes…
  remain readable". Half (a) must stay (the silent-drop guard is the load-bearing
  contract). Half (b) and the comment block (lines 132-145) describing it must be
  deleted; the file-level comment should be re-anchored to say "the consumer
  fallback was retired in v2.4.1; legacy on-disk envelopes carrying ONLY
  `payload.summary` now surface as `null` in `/crews:review-mail` output".

Tests that remain valid (producer-mirror retention):

- `tests/member-reply-notify.test.js:90-93` — asserts both `payload.summary` and
  `payload.kind` exist on the post-stop envelope, then asserts
  `formatReviewMailEntry(note).summary === 'answered 2+2'`. The producer mirror
  still writes both addresses; the formatter reads top-level. Stays green.
- `tests/proactive-report-notify.test.js:58-110` — same pattern for the
  proactive-report notification path. Stays green.
- `tests/integration/cli-spawn-proactive-report.test.js:62` — asserts
  `mailbox[0].payload.kind === 'blocked'`. Stays green (unrelated to summary
  cleanup; the `payload.kind` mirror is out of scope for v2.4.1).

### Technical Constraints

- **No envelope wire format change.** Producer keeps emitting both addresses.
  Consumer simply stops reading the secondary address. Backward-compatible with
  every prior producer version (those wrote both addresses); forward-compatible
  with every consumer that reads top-level only.
- **Strict-mode test pre-existing fixtures.** v2.4.0 flipped
  `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` ON by default in `tests/run.js`. The inverted
  `review-mail-command.test.js` block must NOT trip the silent-drop guard while
  fabricating its payload-only fixture. Use the same per-test opt-out pattern
  already in `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` (process-env
  save-and-restore around the fixture build), or construct the fixture via
  `formatReviewMailEntry` direct call without round-tripping through
  `validateEnvelope`.
- **Patch-bump justification.** No public API change; no on-disk format change;
  no operator-visible behaviour change EXCEPT for the genuinely-rare case of an
  on-disk envelope carrying ONLY `payload.summary` (one without a top-level
  mirror). Such an envelope would only exist if (a) it was written by code
  predating v1.7.3 (May 28 2026) and (b) is still unconsumed in someone's
  mailbox at upgrade time. The probability is negligible given the
  consume-on-read model. Patch bump (v2.4.1) is appropriate.

## Approach

### Architecture

The cleanup is a localized two-line change plus test updates. No new abstractions,
no schema changes, no migration step. The defensive write-then-read dual-path is
collapsed to write-then-canonical-read. The producer mirror is intentionally
RETAINED — not as defensive code, but as the on-disk insurance for the rare
in-flight envelope window described above. A separate future cleanup may revisit
whether the producer mirror itself can be retired (and at that point, the same
analysis must extend to `payload.kind` and to any pre-v2.4.1 readers in operator
side-tooling).

### Implementation Strategy

Single-story execution (US-001). Ordered steps:

1. Edit `hooks/commands/review-mail.js:110` — change
   `summary: row?.summary ?? row?.payload?.summary ?? null,`
   to
   `summary: row?.summary ?? null,`.
2. Update `tests/review-mail-command.test.js:361-378` — invert the assertion: a
   row carrying `payload.summary` but no top-level `summary` now surfaces
   `entry.summary === null`. Add a one-line comment pointing at this plan and at
   the CHANGELOG entry so the next reader understands why the inversion is
   intentional. Pre-existing `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` default in the runner is fine
   for this test because `formatReviewMailEntry` does not call `validateEnvelope`
   on its input row.
3. Update `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` — delete the read-fallback
   half (any sub-block that exercises `formatReviewMailEntry(payloadOnlyRow)` and
   asserts the summary surfaces). Keep half (a), the silent-drop guard, intact;
   it is the load-bearing piece. Update the comment block at lines 129-145 to
   describe the v2.4.1 state: producer mirror retained, consumer fallback retired,
   silent-drop guard remains the authoritative producer-side check.
4. Update `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` header comments — line 7-11's
   "Two-address read fallbacks elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. review-mail.js
   summary fallback) are documented transitional code paths cleared by the
   dedicated cleanup follow-up" should be updated to "The consumer-side
   `review-mail.js` fallback was retired in v2.4.1; the producer mirror at
   `stop.js:1086/1122` is retained as the in-flight on-disk envelope bridge until
   a future cleanup retires both halves together." Line 17-20's TRANSITIONAL
   DUPLICATE note still applies (the mirror is still written, the validator still
   tolerates it when top-level is set); line 192's "follow-up removes
   `payload.summary` entirely" remains accurate as a future statement.
5. Bump `plugins/crews/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `plugins/crews/.github/plugin/plugin.json`,
   and `plugins/crews/CLAUDE.md` version reference (search for `2.4.0` and
   replace with `2.4.1` in version-pinning lines only — do NOT touch CHANGELOG
   history entries for v2.4.0). Bump `plugins/crews/tests/version.test.js` if it
   pins the version string. Add a CHANGELOG `## 2.4.1 - <date>` entry describing
   the consumer-fallback removal.
6. Run `node --check` on edited files and `node tests/run.js` for the crews
   plugin to confirm green under the default `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` runner.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Delete consumer fallback `row?.payload?.summary` at `review-mail.js:110`.
- Update the two tests that codify the fallback.
- Update `envelope.js` header comments to reflect the v2.4.1 state.
- Bump crews to v2.4.1 across all version-pinning sites + CHANGELOG.
- Verify `node tests/run.js` green for the crews plugin under default
  `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1`.

### Out of Scope

- Removing the producer mirror at `stop.js:1086` / `stop.js:1122`. That is the
  "future cleanup" referenced in `envelope.js:192` and is gated on operator
  decision about retiring the on-disk bridge for pre-v2.4.1 envelopes. Separate
  follow-up task.
- Removing the `payload.kind` mirror at `stop.js:1087` / `stop.js:1123`. Zero
  production reader, but `tests/member-reply-notify.test.js:91` and
  `tests/proactive-report-notify.test.js:58/83/109` and
  `tests/integration/cli-spawn-proactive-report.test.js:62` assert it as a
  canonical wire address. Decoupling the kind mirror requires its own design
  decision (delete the assertions vs. promote `payload.kind` to a real reader);
  separate follow-up.
- Renames of asymmetric fields (`payload.replyToId` → `payload.replyTo`,
  `from.kind` → `from.routingKind`). Both flagged in the brainstorm as v2.0.0-scale
  breaking changes; way out of scope for a patch bump.
- The other v1.7.3-era "did this field get a defensive dual-path?" candidates
  (`decision`, `ack`, `bodyResolution`, `reviewedSeq`). All surveyed in the
  brainstorm catalog and re-verified here; none have the dual-path pattern (see
  Survey Findings in `## Open Questions`).
- Adoption of `buildEnvelope` at additional producer call-sites — already done in
  v2.3.2 (`095bba57`).

## Risk Areas

- **In-flight envelope window (LOW).** Between v1.7.3 (deployed May 28 2026) and
  v2.4.1, the producer mirror has been writing both addresses. An on-disk
  envelope that carries ONLY `payload.summary` (no top-level mirror) can only
  predate v1.7.3 (now ~3 days of fork-internal use). After upgrading to v2.4.1,
  any such envelope renders with `summary: null` in `/crews:review-mail` output;
  the prose body still flows through `bodyText(row)` / `resolveBodyFromOutbox`
  and is unaffected. Mitigation: the producer mirror is intentionally kept, so
  any post-v1.7.3 on-disk envelope continues to render correctly.
- **Strict-mode test interaction (LOW).** v2.4.0's `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1`
  runner default could trip `validateEnvelope` if the inverted
  `review-mail-command.test.js` fixture is fed through `buildEnvelope` instead
  of constructed as a plain object. Mitigation: the test already constructs the
  row as a plain object and calls `formatReviewMailEntry` directly (review of
  lines 361-378 confirms this), so no validator invocation occurs. If
  `validateEnvelope` ever becomes a precondition of `formatReviewMailEntry`, the
  test needs the same opt-out pattern documented in `tests/run.js` comment
  block (set `process.env.CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA = '0'` at file top).
- **Operator side-tooling reading `payload.summary` (LOW).** A quick repo-wide
  grep across the entire workspace found ZERO consumers outside
  `hooks/commands/review-mail.js:110`. No bookkeeper script, no codexu lib, no
  Ralph plugin reads `payload.summary`. Removing the fallback affects only the
  documented `/crews:review-mail` JSON output.

## Suggested Decomposition

Single cluster; serial execution. No parallelism opportunity — the change is
fewer than ~30 LoC across one production file, two test files, three
metadata/doc files, and one CHANGELOG.

- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`hooks/commands/review-mail.js`,

  `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` (comments only), `CHANGELOG.md`, three

- `execution_mode` rationale: trivial single-story scope; parallelizing would

## Open Questions

### Survey of other v1.7.3-era fields (no further cleanup recommended)

The spawn prompt asked whether the v1.7.3 dual-path pattern was applied to other
fields. The brainstorm at
`.ralph/brainstorms/crews-summary-rendering-audit/selected-direction.md` ran a
three-lens (codex + copilot + devils-advocate) catalog at v1.7.3; this plan
re-verified each field against the v2.4.0 HEAD:

| Field | Defensive dual-path? | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `summary` | **YES** — producer mirror at `stop.js:1086/1122` + consumer fallback at `review-mail.js:110`. | THIS CLEANUP. |
| `kind` | NO — `row.kind` and `row.from.kind` are semantically distinct (report kind vs routing kind), not a defensive mirror. Consumer at `review-mail.js:84-89` reads `row.kind \|\| row.from.kind` for legitimate reasons. The `payload.kind` mirror at `stop.js:1087/1123` is write-only (no production reader). | OUT OF SCOPE; backlog candidate "evaluate retirement of `payload.kind` mirror". |
| `replyTo` / `payload.replyToId` | NO — intentional two-address asymmetry on two distinct message types (outbox vs member-reply system-mailbox notification), codified in `envelope.js:24-31` and asserted by `tests/member-reply-notify.test.js:89`. Not a defensive mirror. | OUT OF SCOPE; brainstorm flagged v2.0.0 rename as separate task `crews-envelope-replyto-field-name-unification`. |
| `decision` | NO — lives on dedicated decision rows at one canonical address only. Never on the envelope. | OUT OF SCOPE; nothing to clean. |
| `ack` | NO — tag-only field on the producer side, transformed to `decision = 'ack-no-action'` on persist. Not an envelope field. | OUT OF SCOPE; nothing to clean. |
| `progressTail` | NO — payload-nested only at `payload.progressTail`. `envelope.js:222-224` explicitly REJECTS top-level `progressTail`. Producer and consumer both read/write the nested address. | OUT OF SCOPE; nothing to clean. |
| `reviewedSeq` | NO — manifest-resident field, not envelope. | OUT OF SCOPE. |
| `bodyResolution` | NO — synthesized client-side by `formatReviewMailEntry` from `resolveBodyFromOutbox(row).status`. Not a wire field. | OUT OF SCOPE. |

### Backlog candidates this plan does not address

1. **`payload.kind` mirror retirement.** Same shape as `payload.summary`: write-mirrored
   at `stop.js:1087/1123`, but the consumer side reads `row.from.kind` (routing)
   not `row.payload.kind`. Tests at `tests/member-reply-notify.test.js:91`,
   `tests/proactive-report-notify.test.js:58/83/109`,
   `tests/integration/cli-spawn-proactive-report.test.js:62` assert the
   on-the-wire mirror exists; removing the mirror requires removing or inverting
   those assertions too. Worth a separate brainstorm to decide whether
   `payload.kind` should be promoted to a real reader address or retired
   entirely.
2. **Producer mirror retirement for `summary`.** The follow-up referenced at
   `envelope.js:192` ("The cleanup follow-up removes `payload.summary`
   entirely"). Gated on operator comfort with abandoning the in-flight on-disk
   bridge. Worth pairing with the `payload.kind` decision since both write
   sites are co-located in `stop.js:1077-1089` / `:1117-1137`.
